items.title: The Intan
items.description: \u003cp\u003eOwner and curator Alvin Yapp has transformed his home into a museum dedicated to the Peranakan culture, with a hoard of fascinating artefacts.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Eurasian Heritage Gallery
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLearn about the history of the Eurasian community in Singapore across the three galleries of this quaint heritage attraction.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Colourful Shophouses along Koon Seng Road
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSnap a shot for Instagram at these iconic, pastel-hued houses. Fun fact: they date back to the 1920s and were inhabited by a diverse community, including the Peranakan Chinese.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Katong Antique House
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThe private museum is a trove of Peranakan antiques ranging from furniture to intricately crafted \u003ci\u003eNyonya\u003c/i\u003e costumes like \u003ci\u003esarong kebaya\u003c/i\u003e and \u003ci\u003ekasut-manek\u003c/i\u003e (beaded shoes).\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Katong-Joo Chiat - Nyonyas, Babas and Peranakan Tour
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover the old-school architecture, charming shophouses and bustling atmosphere of the neighbourhood from the sidecar of a vintage Vespa.\u003c/p\u003e\r
items.image: https://www.visitsingapore.com/content/dam/visitsingapore/neighbourhoods/katong-joo-chiat/updated/title-slider/Joo Chiat + Katong - Nyonyas, Babas and Peranakan_Option 1_Source Singapore Sidecars-544x544.jpg

items.title: Sri Senpaga Vinayagar Temple
items.description: \u003cp\u003eOne of the oldest Hindu temples in Singapore, its four granite pillars, etched entrance stone, and unique musical pillar offers visitors a captivating journey through centuries of tradition and devotion.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Cat Socrates
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBrowse through a host of books and knick-knacks at this cool indie retail shop,\u0026nbsp;Cat Socrates—and say hi to the resident cats!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kim Choo Kueh Chang
items.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom delicious \u003ci\u003eNyonya\u003c/i\u003e \u003ci\u003ekueh\u003c/i\u003e and dumplings to exquisite dresses and jewellery, this beloved store has been selling all things Peranakan since 1945.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Hat of Cain
items.description: \u003cp\u003eGet dapper and show off your style at Hat of Cain, which specialises in authentic, handwoven hats from Ecuador for both men and women.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Onlewo
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTake home a piece of Singapore with you. The trinkets, gifts\u0026nbsp;and home-decor items from Onlewo are inspired by iconic local neighbourhoods, wildlife and motifs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Rumah Bebe
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLearn the intricacies of Peranakan beadwork or peruse a selection of finely crafted wares at this colourful establishment.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Quentin\u0027s Eurasian Restaurant
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into comfort food with an Eurasian twist at this beloved\u0026nbsp;restaurant. From hearty corned beef rice and fried okra to fiery curry debal (or devil curry), the dishes here are bound to sate your appetite.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kway Guan Huat Joo Chiat Popiah
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLearn how the beloved local dish popiah is made at this eight-decade old family-run store, which was a recipient of Stewards of Intangible Cultural Heritage Award in 2020.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Guan Hoe Soon
items.description: \u003cp\u003eIndulge in delectable dishes like \u003ci\u003eayam buah keluak\u003c/i\u003e (chicken with black nut gravy),\u003ci\u003e ikan assam pedas\u003c/i\u003e (fish in a sour and spicy tamarind gravy) and \u003ci\u003eotak-otak\u003c/i\u003e (grilled fish cake with coconut milk and spices), at Singapore’s oldest Peranakan eatery.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Big Short Coffee
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAt Big Short Coffee, coffees are crafted with scientific precision and cocktail creativity, featuring a rotating menu that changes every few months.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Birds of Paradise Gelato Boutique
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThe ideal dessert pitstop, this Michelin-recommended local gelato brand serves up a range of unique, botanically-inspired flavours, from white chrysanthemum to vanilla fig.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: The Original Katong Laksa
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into this savoury home-grown noodle dish, with a broth made from coconut milk and ingredients like\u0026nbsp;cockles, prawns and fishcake.\u003c/p\u003e\r \u003cp\u003eThe version at Katong can\u0026nbsp;be easily slurped up with a spoon - no chopsticks needed!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Old Bibik’s Peranakan Kitchen
items.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom humble hawker beginnings in 2009, Old Bibik Peranakan Kitchen is a Joo Chiat gem serving vibrant, MSG-free Peranakan dishes rich in heritage and hearty flavours.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Hotel Indigo
items.description: \u003cp\u003eImmerse in the local Peranakan culture at the quaint\u0026nbsp;Hotel Indigo, which fuses retro décor with modern swank.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Santa Grand Hotel
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHoused in a building that embodies Chinese Baroque architecture, this hotel offers the best of both worlds, with its charming heritage and modern amenities.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chinatown Heritage Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eStep back in time at Chinatown Heritage Centre, rebuilt from memories of early residents who lived in these shophouses. Immerse in their stories of struggles and dreams.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Smith Street
items.description: \u003cp\u003eExperience Smith Street, where Chinatown\u0027s heritage meets modern energy through traditional shops, eateries, creative spaces, and cultural activities that bring traditions to life.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chinatown Murders (牛车水 Murders)
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis murder mystery tour through Chinatown is filled with intriguing clues and untold stories.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Trails of Tan Ah Huat
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHop on a bicycle and let Tan Ah Huat – a fictitious coolie – bring the streets of Chinatown to life.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Growing Up - A Mural Walk in Chinatown
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover Chinatown\u0027s past with an art walk featuring murals by Yip Yew Chong. Don’t forget to snap away!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple \u0026 Museum
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHome to a sacred relic, this majestic temple is a trove of Buddhist wisdom.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Masjid Jamae
items.description: \u003cp\u003eOne of our city\u0027s oldest mosques, Masjid Jamae is famous for its eastern and western infused architecture.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Sri Mariamman Temple
items.description: \u003cp\u003eStep into Singapore’s oldest Hindu temple to admire the ornate carvings and soak in the vibrant atmosphere.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Thian Hock Keng Temple
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSingapore’s oldest Chinese temple is steeped in heritage and\u0026nbsp;is a must-visit for history aficionados.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Singapore Art Museum
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSingapore\u0027s pioneering art museum is home to the work of bright young artists and regional names alike.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chinatown Street Market
items.description: \u003cp\u003eMore than just a shopping stretch, this iconic street is home to a wide range of offerings, from lacquered fans to charming souvenirs.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Yue Hwa Building
items.description: \u003cp\u003eGo treasure hunting in Yue Hwa building – this charming department store is chock full of anything you\u0027d desire, from traditional herbs and calligraphy brushes to tasty snacks.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bee Cheng Hiang
items.description: \u003cp\u003eWith humble street hawker roots that date back to the 1930s, Bee Cheng Hiang serves up delicious slices of freshly barbecued meat.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kele
items.description: \u003cp\u003eStarting out as a humble bakery nearly four decades ago, Kele is now one of Singapore\u0027s most popular snack brands. Sample their pineapple tarts and savour the tradition!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Pek Sin Choon
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTalk about an old-school pick me up. Pek Sin Choon has been selling its range of fragrant, traditional tea for almost a century.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: On Cheong Jewellery
items.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom jade bangles and gold necklaces to beautifully-crafted rings, this traditional jeweller boasts a range of masterful designs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Binary Style
items.description: \u003cp\u003eShop from a homegrown lifestyle brand, renowned for its vibrant prints inspired by local architecture and nature.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chop Wah On
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSoothe your aches at Chop Wah On, one of Singapore\u0027s oldest medicated oil makers. Since 1916, this family business crafts healing remedies and traditional balms.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Eu Yan Sang
items.description: \u003cp\u003eExperience traditional wellness at Eu Yan Sang, a trusted name in Chinese medicine for over 145 years. Discover time-tested herbal remedies and wellness products.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chinatown Complex
items.description: \u003cp\u003eEat your way through the delectable dishes at Chinatown Complex, Singapore\u0027s largest food centre. Keep your eye out for the Michelin Bib Gourmand-awarded hawker stalls!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Maxwell Food Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eA beloved stomping ground of local foodies, Maxwell Food Centre is home to hawker delights like chicken rice.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: No Sleep Club
items.description: \u003cp\u003eRanked 15 on 2023\u0027s list of Asia\u0027s 50 Best Bars, No Sleep Club is the perfect spot for coffee, cocktails or bar food with an elevated twist.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Zen
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBjorn Frantzén\u0027s three Michelin-starred restaurant is famed for its masterful take on Scandinavian and Japanese fusion cuisine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Native
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSample the flavours of Asia at one of Asia\u0027s 50 Best Bars – the unique cocktails here are concocted with ingredients and spirits from Singapore and across the region.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Tong Heng Traditional Cantonese Pastries
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSome of the toothsome pastries from Tong Heng include candied melon pastries, savoury buns and their signature egg tarts.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kok Sen Restaurant
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis Michelin Bib Gourmand-awarded restaurant is run by the\u0026nbsp;third generation and serves up a tantalising range of Cantonese cuisine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Restaurant Espoir
items.description: \u003cp\u003eRestaurant Espoir blends European culinary artistry with bold flavours of Malayan herbs and spices, offering a modern Halal dining experience with delightful surprises in every bite.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Clan Hotel
items.description: \u003cp\u003eModern luxury meets old-school heritage in the heart of Chinatown, with Clan Hotel\u0027s immaculate service and well-appointed rooms.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering, Singapore
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBesides exquisite amenities and world-class hospitality, PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering, Singapore is famed for its award-winning designs for sustainability.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Hajjah Fatimah Mosque
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAlso known as Masjid Hajjah Fatimah, the Hajjah Fatimah Mosque will captivate you with its blend of cross-cultural architectural influences.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: #instawalk: Bugis, Waterloo, Kampong Gelam
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTake a jaunt around Bugis, Waterloo Street and Kampong Gelam, explore hidden gems and snap a trove of Instagram-worthy shots for your social media feeds.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Haji Lane
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSingapore\u0027s original indie neighbourhood is a great place to wander, with its hole-in-the-wall bars, boutique fashion stores and indie businesses. Keep a look out for wall murals and graffiti by both local and internationally-renowned artists.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: A Painted Sip
items.description: \u003cp\u003eA beginner-friendly immersive painting workshop where participants can paint and customise their own reusable tumblers and choose from a range of Singapore-inspired designs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kebaya by Ratianah
items.description: \u003cp\u003eMasterfully-tailored from exquisite fabric, the \u003ci\u003ekebaya\u003c/i\u003e and the \u003ci\u003ebaju kurung\u003c/i\u003e from Ratianah Tahir\u0027s boutique are bound to brighten up your wardrobe.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Jamal Kazura Aromatics
items.description: \u003cp\u003eFall in love with the world of perfume at Jamal Kazura Aromatics, a traditional perfumery that\u0027s been around since 1933. Discover a perfume that speaks to your personality or create your own signature scent.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Hygge
items.description: \u003cp\u003eClassical designs and elegant minimalism exude from the trinkets, accessories and decor on display at Hygge. Take home a dose of cosiness, and find the ideal gift for your loved ones at home.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Crafune
items.description: \u003cp\u003eGet inspired to work with your hands, and pick up basics of leather-working at Crafune, where you can learn how to make your very own accessories, from wallets to handbags.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bugis Street
items.description: \u003cp\u003eA bustling street market that sells everything from quirky knick knacks to fashionable garments. Scour the best deals through shops packed with clothes, shoes and accessories.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Goodluck Bunch
items.description: \u003cp\u003eIf you\u0027re a fan of street culture, you\u0027re going to love the effortlessly cool vibes at Goodluck Bunch, with its selection of hoodies, sneakers and apparel for both men and women.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Toko Aljunied
items.description: \u003cp\u003eIntricate\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003ebatik\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003efabrics and gorgeous, hand-sewn garments are on display at this traditional store, with a history that dates all the way back to 1940.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Hjh Maimunah
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into food that tastes just like your \u003ci\u003emakcik\u003c/i\u003e (aunty) made it at Hjh Maimunah. This Michelin Bib Gourmand eatery is famous for its \u003ci\u003enasi padang\u003c/i\u003e – rice with an assortment of delicious side dishes, from beef \u003ci\u003erendang\u003c/i\u003e to \u003ci\u003esambal \u003c/i\u003eprawns.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Rumah Makan Minang
items.description: \u003cp\u003eRun by the third generation, the rich and diverse flavours of Indonesian cuisine are on full display at Rumah Makan Minang. Enjoy delicious traditional fare like\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003etahu telur\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003eand\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003emee soto.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: The Coconut Club
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into a plate of\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003enasi lemak\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003e– a traditional rice dish made with a variety of side ingredients. The version whipped up by The Coconut Club, a Michelin Bib Gourmand recipient, elevates this hawker staple with a modern spin on its ingredients.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bar Stories
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis cozy\u0026nbsp;watering hole offers bespoke cocktails to thirsty tipplers, with a variety of drinks inspired by your response to the bartenders\u0027 questions.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Ji Xiang Ang Ku Kueh
items.description: \u003cp\u003eJi Xiang is a local brand that specializes in Ang Ku Kueh, a traditional Chinese pastry made with soft and chewy glutinous rice flour. Located right opposite Bugis Junction, this store is one of its 10 outlets in Singapore.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Lou Shang
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLou Shang, which means \u0026quot;upstairs\u0026quot; in English, is a cafe that offers a trip down memory lane through its nostalgic decor and locally inspired menu. It is located at Prinsep Street in the Bras Basah and Bugis precinct.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bugis HaveFun LiveShow
items.description: \u003cp\u003eImmerse yourself in the electrifying atmosphere at HaveFun Live Show at Bugis+. Enjoy an unforgettable night with bar delights and close-up live performances!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: The Sultan
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAdmire the columns and full-length shuttered French windows of the conserved buildings that houses The Sultan, and then step inside to immerse yourself in a world of comfort.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Andaz Singapore
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTreat yourself to thoughtfully designed guestrooms with stunning views of the city, at the first Andaz-branded property in Southeast Asia.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Sri Veerakaliamman Temple
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBuilt by Indian pioneers living in the Serangoon district in the 19th century, this gorgeous place of worship is dedicated to Kali the Hindu goddess and destroyer of evil.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Indian Heritage Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eIndian Heritage Centre\u0027s galleries and artefacts tell the enthralling story of Singapore\u0027s Indian community. The venue\u0026nbsp;also houses a Singapore Visitor Centre where you can pick up handy information.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Former House of Tan Teng Niah
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBuilt in 1900, the\u0026nbsp;former house of Tan Teng Niah is a 2-storey villa with rainbow-hued exteriors that make for the perfect photo opportunity.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Tea \u0026 Tiffin: Cultural \u0026 Food Tour of Little India
items.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover the tale of our country\u0027s Indian pioneers, tastes of tradition and our evolving cityscape on this vibrant and colourful tour with the masterful guides from Culture Curious.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Mustafa Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eNo trip to Little India is complete without a visit to this massive department store, which sells everything from jewelry to groceries and electronics.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Jothi Store and Flower Shop
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBesides flower garlands and prayer items sold for religious occasions, this store is filled with a range of traditional Indian beauty products, homeware, kitchenware and other colourful souvenirs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Little India Arcade
items.description: \u003cp\u003eA bustling area filled with an array of boutique shops and eateries. Discover henna art at Selvi\u0027s Beauty Salon, browse the goods at Gokulam Jewels and Craft, and indulge in dishes from Apolo\u0027s Food Village.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Haniffa
items.description: \u003cp\u003eOriginally specialising in\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003esaris\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003eand textiles when it opened in 1962, this traditional merchant now sells a variety of jewellery, electronics and other goods.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Tekka Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTekka Centre is Singapore’s largest indoor ‘wet’ market, selling an incredible array of fresh produce, aromatic spices and dried goods.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Banana Leaf Apolo
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLocated along\u0026nbsp;Race Course Road, Banana Leaf Apolo is popular for its spread of delicious South Indian food. Be sure to sample the famous local delicacy, fish head curry on banana leaf.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bismillah Biryani
items.description: \u003cp\u003eA six-time Michelin Bib Gourmand Award Winner, this heritage restaurant doles out aromatic portions of authentic\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003edum biryani,\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003ea traditional rice dish.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Olibier Rooftop Bar
items.description: \u003cp\u003eKick back, relax with a cold beer or craft cocktails and enjoy the view at this laid-back rooftop bar. Expect chill tunes from live DJ sets and even a roving fortune teller on occasion.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Podi \u0026 Poriyal

items.title: Pulau Ubin
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLocated on the eastern end of Singapore, hitch a bumboat ride to find rustic shrines, swamplands and scenic summits.\u003c/p\u003e\r \u003cp\u003eThis sanctuary is the perfect place for explorers looking to unwind and deepen their love for nature.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Mangrove Kayaking
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBeginner friendly, this guided tour allows you to explore the Pulau Ubin\u0027s tranquil environment and abundance of floral and fauna whilst paddling on kayaks.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chek Jawa
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTucked away in the east of Pulau Ubin, this rich intertidal ecosystem is home to diverse wildlife. Head to the Jewawi Tower for a chance to observe birds and a panoramic view of the island.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Lazarus Island
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAs an alternative to Pulau Ubin Island, bask in the sun, sand, and sea at Lazarus Island. This hidden gem boasts relaxing beaches and abundant marine life, just a ferry ride away from the mainland.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Singapore Botanic Gardens
items.description: \u003cp\u003eRecognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, find highlights such as National Orchid Garden, a gorgeous swan lake and heaps of tropical trees to please every plant enthusiast out there.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve
items.description: \u003cp\u003eWhile the sun’s still out, check out this reserve to find Singapore’s highest hill, Bukit Timah Hill. Challenge yourself to a trek up its 163-metre-high slopes, on trails that wind through pockets of forested area.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Southern Ridges
items.description: \u003cp\u003eKeep your camera on hand when you hike the photogenic ten-kilometre-long network of trails. Head to Henderson Waves, the highest pedestrian bridge in Singapore.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: MacRitchie Nature Trail and Reservoir Park
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThe highlight of this park is its Treetop Walks, a 250-metre aerial free standing suspension bridge spanning the two highest points within MacRitchie.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: AltitudeX
items.description: \u003cp\u003eExperience the world’s largest wind tunnel for indoor skydiving. State-of-the-art technology will lend you wings in an experience that simulates free falls from heights of 12,000 to 3,000 feet.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Mega Adventure Park
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBrave new heights with this adrenaline-pumping zip wire ride, where you will get to experience a whole new perspective of Sentosa\u0027s lush jungles and white beaches from 450 metres in the air.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Hydrodash
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLocated along the waters of Palawan Beach, Singapore’s first floating aquapark is an unforgettable experience for the young and the young at heart.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Skyline Luge
items.description: \u003cp\u003eEmbark on a thrilling journey as you zoom down thrilling courses in a 3-wheeled luge.\u003c/p\u003e\r \u003cp\u003eThe skyride also offers a magnificent bird’s eye view of the city.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Adventure Cove
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHave a splashing good time at Adventure Cove, experience thrilling water slides, snorkel with fish, and relax on the lazy river.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Gardens By the Bay
items.description: \u003cp\u003eGardens by the Bay is a stunning park consisting of three waterfront gardens. Discover rare flowers, Supertrees, and intriguing sculptures from all over the world.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Trifecta
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSurf, snow and skate in one destination! This integrated facility in Orchard Road will offer a wave of excitement for both beginners and seasoned professionals.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Climb Central Funan
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAscend to new heights with rock climbing located in the centre of this trendy mall. Pick between high intensity short climbs or scale the many high walls.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Slingshot
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis thrilling ride catapults you\u0026nbsp;nearly 70 metres up in the air, at speeds of over 160 kilometres per hour. Enjoy the breezy nightscape of the Singapore River while screaming at the top of your lungs!\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Singapore DuckTours
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSpend your first day in Singapore sampling all that our city has to offer with this hop-on and hop-off ride. Some highlights include Little India, Orchard Road and Chinatown.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: National Gallery
items.description: \u003cp\u003eVisit the world\u0027s largest public display of modern Southeast Asian art. Stroller friendly, it also houses the Keppel Centre for Art Education, a children-centric learning zone that revolves around the themes of art and wonder.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: ArtScience Museum
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis beloved lotus-inspired establishment blurs the lines between art, science, culture and technology, with exciting hands-on and interactive exhibitions on rotation that are perfect for children.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Singapore River Cruise
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThen, make your way to a traditional bumboat. Let your guide engage the whole family in a captivating tale of Singapore’s two famous quays—Boat Quay and Clarke Quay—and take in the scenic views.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Children’s Museum
items.description: \u003cp\u003eGot little ones in tow? Don’t miss the Children’s Museum Singapore! It is interactive, playful, and totally worth the visit if you’ve got energetic kids who love to explore.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Sentosa
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSpend the whole day at Sentosa, a playground for the whole family. There’s something for everyone on this island at Southern Singapore, including a giant floating water park - Hydrodash, with designated zones for kids.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Universal Studios Singapore
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis movie-themed entertainment park is peppered with thrilling rides based on blockbuster flicks like Transformers and Jurassic Park.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Skyline Luge
items.description: \u003cp\u003eFeel your adrenaline pumping while riding this 3-wheeled luge carts down windy tracks, that\u0027s great for both the young and young at heart.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kiztopia Prestige
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHead to Kiztopia Prestige in River Valley, a premium play space made just for your little ones! Discover fun play zones with soft play areas and interactive programs in a safe environment.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Science Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eExplore a world of discovery at Science Centre Singapore, where hands-on exhibits, imaginative play at KidsSTOP™, and immersive 8K 3D dome experiences at the Omni-Theatre inspire curious minds of all ages to learn and imagine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Singapore Botanic Gardens
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTake a stroll at Singapore’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site. Check out highlights like the Swan Lake and National Orchid Garden, which is home to the world’s largest display of orchids.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Jacob Ballas Children\u0027s Gardens
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThe first garden in Asia dedicated to children, this park allows children to explore, play and have an adventure, while learning and cultivating a love for nature.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Dempsey
items.description: \u003cp\u003eWithin the greenery of the Dempsey neighbourhood, you will find great spots for families to unwind - like PS. Cafe, which offers Modern European creations, and the Museum of Ice Cream, where children two and under can enter for free.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Orchard Road
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHead over to Orchard Road, a world-famous shopping district. The area is home to family-friendly shopping malls, Paragon and Ngee Ann City, with plenty of shopping for both children and adults.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Singapore Zoo
items.description: \u003cp\u003eObserve animals in their natural habits at the Singapore Zoo. Indulge in a hearty Breakfast in the Wild, which will have you dining alongside Orangutans and Macaws, perfect for all animal lovers.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Bird Paradise
items.description: \u003cp\u003ePop by adjacent Bird Paradise, home to over 3,500 birds, with highlights including walk through aviaries that reflect habitats across the world.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: River Wonders
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAlternatively, head to a river-themed zoo and aquarium to find animals like the Giant Panda, Brazilian Tapirs and Capybara.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Night Safari
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAs dusk falls, head to the Night Safari for a world of nocturnal creatures. Explore the park on a Safari Tram Adventure or head to the walking trails to see the animals up close.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Amoy Street Market
items.description: \u003cp\u003eWith a name that means \u0027little rebel\u0027 in Chinese, this restaurant serves up playful renditions of fusion fare, and local classics with an elevated twist. \u003ci\u003eSatay\u003c/i\u003e made with Angus Beef and Roast Duck flavoured with truffle are just some highlights on its colourful menu.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Maxwell Food Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHoused in a traditional Chinese shophouse, this restaurant and cocktail bar pays homage to Singapore’s rich history with its reinterpretation of classic dishes and cocktails with a Singaporean flavour.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Chinatown Complex Food Centre
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBorn from a humble hawker stall in 1992, Harummanis has evolved into a culinary journey led by Akmal Anuar. Honouring his parents\u0027 30 year legacy, Akmal puts a modern touch on traditional Malay food.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: GINLEE Studio
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSustainability is at the heart of this brand\u0027s philosophy, with designs made from sustainable fabrics like Tencel and hands-on workshops to redesign customers\u0027 old apparel.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Studio Gypsied
items.description: \u003cp\u003eSlow fashion is the byword with this brand, with sustainably sourced batik that\u0027s made-to-order by traditional artisans from marginalised communities.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Esse
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTimeless design and sustainability harmonise at Esse, with designs made from organic and renewable fabrics.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: The Green Collective
items.description: \u003cp\u003eA curation of sustainable brands, The Green Collective sells everything from candles to food and fashion, and also hosts sustainable workshops.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: The Sustainability Project
items.description: \u003cp\u003eMore than just a store, this retail brand is a movement. You\u0027ll find sustainable items like straws and cutlery, but also workshops and zero waste initiatives.\u003c/p\u003e\r \u003cp\u003e\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Fysh
items.description: \u003cp\u003eHelmed by Josh Niland, FYSH brings a revolutionary, sustainable approach to whole fish cooking. Using the finest ingredients, each dish celebrates often-overlooked components for a unique and responsible dining experience.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Restaurant Air CCCC
items.description: \u003cp\u003eAIR redefines sustainable dining with its holistic Awareness, Impact and Responsibility ethos. Nestled in Dempsey Hill, it combines farm-to-table produce with an innovative approach for a mindful culinary experience.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Scaled by Ah Hua Kelong
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTaste the freshness of the sea\u0027s bounty at Scaled, which sources its seafood from local farmers, instead of seafood imported from overseas.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Laurus Table
items.description: \u003cp\u003eLaurus Table marries the elegance of Italy’s Amalfi Coast with Singapore’s coastal bounty. Savour fresh seafood and sustainably farmed fish, complemented by organic produce and herbs handpicked from The Laurus’s own garden.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Level 33
items.description: \u003cp\u003eRevel in artisanal beer, fine dining and stunning views at the world\u0027s highest microbrewery. Serving sustainably produced beers and incorporating brewing byproducts into its dishes, each mouthful is a delight to the senses and planet.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Kaarla and Oumi @1-Arden
items.description: \u003cp\u003eBoth sister restaurants source\u0026nbsp;sustainable produce from local farms and right outside their doorstep, at the 10,000 square foot 1-Arden Food Forest.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Seroja
items.description: \u003cp\u003eWinner of the Michelin Green Star, this restaurant foregrounds dishes from the Malay Archipelago, with local seafood, produce and spices.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Ugly Food Tour Through Jalan Besar (Sinful Bites and Bright Lights)
items.description: \u003cp\u003eMinimise your carbon footprint by hoofing it on a walking tour, as you learn about Jalan Besar\u0027s colourful history and delicious hawker fare.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Sentosa Intertidal Exploration
items.description: \u003cp\u003eGet inspired to do\u0026nbsp;your\u003cb\u003e\u0026nbsp;\u003c/b\u003epart for the planet\u0026nbsp;by admiring the intricate ecosystems and habitats on the sunny island of Sentosa.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Culture, Art and Architecture Private Tour
items.description: \u003cp\u003eTake a walk down memory lane and learn how local artists depicted Singapore, as you explore Chinatown and the heart of the city.\u003c/p\u003e\r

items.title: Historical Singapore Bicycle Tour
items.description: \u003cp\u003eThis eco-friendly bike tour will take you on a meandering ride down the Singapore River, as you discover mosques, museums and other fascinating landmarks.\u003c/p\u003e\r
